subject: Gastrointestinal
subtopic: Biliary tract disease: PSC, PBC, secondary biliary cirrhosis
vignette: A 45-year-old man with ulcerative colitis has fatigue, jaundice, and pruritus. MRCP shows alternating strictures and dilations of the intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts, giving a beaded appearance.
question: Which of the following best explains these biliary findings?

options.text: Primary sclerosing cholangitis with concentric onion-skin bile duct fibrosis
Primary biliary cholangitis with lymphocytic destruction of lobular bile ducts
Secondary biliary cirrhosis caused by an obstructing pancreatic carcinoma
Choledocholithiasis with a single gallstone in the common bile duct
Autoimmune hepatitis with interface hepatitis

explanation_correct: Primary sclerosing cholangitis causes concentric onion-skin bile duct fibrosis, producing alternating strictures and dilation with beading of intra- and extrahepatic ducts on ERCP or MRCP. It classically affects middle-aged males with ulcerative colitis; p-ANCA/MPO positivity and elevated IgM are associated. It can progress to secondary biliary cirrhosis and increases the risk of cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer.

explanation_incorrect.B: Primary biliary cholangitis destroys lobular bile ducts, is associated with antimitochondrial antibody in middle-aged women, and does not produce beading.
explanation_incorrect.C: Secondary biliary cirrhosis follows extrahepatic obstruction without the diffuse beading of PSC.
explanation_incorrect.D: Choledocholithiasis produces obstruction and cholestatic enzymes but not diffuse beading of the biliary tree.
explanation_incorrect.E: Autoimmune hepatitis is a hepatocellular pattern of injury, not a fibrotic biliary stricturing disease.

educationalObjective: PSC features onion-skin fibrosis and beaded ducts on ERCP/MRCP in middle-aged men with ulcerative colitis.

subject: Gastrointestinal
subtopic: Biliary tract disease: PSC, PBC, secondary biliary cirrhosis
vignette: A 50-year-old woman has fatigue and pruritus. Laboratory testing shows an elevated alkaline phosphatase and positive antimitochondrial antibodies.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
Primary biliary cholangitis
Secondary biliary cirrhosis
Autoimmune hepatitis
Hemochromatosis

explanation_correct: Primary biliary cholangitis is an autoimmune lymphocytic destruction of lobular bile ducts, with or without granulomas, classically affecting middle-aged women. Antimitochondrial antibody is positive and IgM is elevated; it is associated with other autoimmune conditions such as Hashimoto thyroiditis, rheumatoid arthritis, and celiac disease. Ursodiol is used for treatment.

explanation_incorrect.A: Primary sclerosing cholangitis affects middle-aged men with ulcerative colitis, is p-ANCA associated, and lacks antimitochondrial antibody.
explanation_incorrect.C: Secondary biliary cirrhosis follows extrahepatic obstruction, not autoimmune lobular bile duct destruction.
explanation_incorrect.D: Autoimmune hepatitis has a hepatocellular enzyme pattern and interface hepatitis, not antimitochondrial antibodies.
explanation_incorrect.E: Hemochromatosis is an iron-overload disease with bronze diabetes, not a cholestatic autoimmune bile duct disease.

educationalObjective: PBC is autoimmune destruction of lobular bile ducts in middle-aged women, marked by antimitochondrial antibodies and treated with ursodiol.

subject: Gastrointestinal
subtopic: Biliary tract disease: PSC, PBC, secondary biliary cirrhosis
vignette: A 52-year-old man with long-standing ulcerative colitis and known biliary stricturing disease is being counseled about his risk of malignancy.
question: For which of the following complications is this patient at distinctly increased risk?

options.text: Hepatocellular carcinoma due to cirrhosis from any cause
Gallbladder cancer due to a porcelain gallbladder
Cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer
Pancreatic adenocarcinoma due to chronic pancreatitis
Hepatic angiosarcoma due to vinyl chloride exposure

explanation_correct: Primary sclerosing cholangitis is associated with ulcerative colitis, p-ANCA/MPO positivity, and elevated IgM, and it carries a distinctly increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer. It can also lead to secondary biliary cirrhosis. This patient's ulcerative colitis plus biliary stricturing disease points strongly to PSC.

explanation_incorrect.A: Hepatocellular carcinoma risk is most emphasized in hemochromatosis and chronic viral hepatitis; PSC's signature malignancies are biliary.
explanation_incorrect.B: Porcelain gallbladder is a gallbladder cancer risk, but this patient has UC-associated stricturing disease rather than a calcified gallbladder.
explanation_incorrect.D: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma risk is linked to chronic pancreatitis, tobacco, and pancreatic head tumors, not PSC.
explanation_incorrect.E: Hepatic angiosarcoma is associated with vinyl chloride and arsenic exposure, not biliary stricturing disease.

educationalObjective: PSC, associated with ulcerative colitis, increases the risk of cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer.

subject: Gastrointestinal
subtopic: Biliary tract disease: PSC, PBC, secondary biliary cirrhosis
vignette: A 60-year-old woman with a history of gallstones presents with jaundice, pruritus, dark urine, and pale stools. Imaging shows obstruction of the common bile duct. Liver biopsy shows fibrosis around intrahepatic ducts and bile stasis.
question: Which of the following best explains the liver findings?

options.text: Autoimmune lymphocytic destruction of lobular bile ducts with granulomas
Concentric onion-skin fibrosis of bile ducts with beading on cholangiography
Iron deposition with bridging fibrosis
Extrahepatic biliary obstruction raising intrahepatic duct pressure, causing injury, fibrosis, and bile stasis
Misfolded alpha-1 antitrypsin accumulating in hepatocytes with PAS-positive globules

explanation_correct: Secondary biliary cirrhosis results from extrahepatic biliary obstruction (eg, gallstones, biliary strictures, pancreatic carcinoma) that raises pressure in intrahepatic ducts, leading to injury, fibrosis, and bile stasis. It may be complicated by acute cholangitis. Cholestatic LFTs show elevated conjugated bilirubin, cholesterol, ALP, and GGT.

explanation_incorrect.A: Lymphocytic destruction of lobular bile ducts with granulomas describes primary biliary cholangitis, not obstruction.
explanation_incorrect.B: Onion-skin fibrosis with beading describes primary sclerosing cholangitis, which is not due to a discrete extrahepatic obstruction.
explanation_incorrect.C: Iron deposition describes hemochromatosis and would not follow common bile duct obstruction.
explanation_incorrect.E: PAS-positive globules from misfolded alpha-1 antitrypsin describe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, not cholestatic fibrosis.

educationalObjective: Secondary biliary cirrhosis follows extrahepatic obstruction (stones, strictures, pancreatic cancer) that raises intrahepatic duct pressure and causes fibrosis and bile stasis.

subject: Gastrointestinal
subtopic: Biliary tract disease: PSC, PBC, secondary biliary cirrhosis
vignette: A patient with a cholestatic biliary tract disease undergoes liver function testing.
question: Which of the following laboratory patterns is most characteristic of a cholestatic biliary tract disease?

options.text: Elevated unconjugated bilirubin, elevated LDH, low haptoglobin
Elevated AST and ALT with normal alkaline phosphatase and GGT
Isolated elevated unconjugated bilirubin with normal alkaline phosphatase
Low albumin and prolonged prothrombin time with normal bilirubin
Elevated conjugated bilirubin, cholesterol, alkaline phosphatase, and GGT

explanation_correct: Biliary tract disease typically produces a cholestatic pattern of liver function tests: elevated conjugated bilirubin, elevated cholesterol, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and elevated GGT. Clinically these patients may have pruritus, jaundice, dark urine, light-colored stools, and hepatosplenomegaly.

explanation_incorrect.A: Elevated unconjugated bilirubin with high LDH and low haptoglobin is hemolysis, not cholestasis.
explanation_incorrect.B: A hepatocellular pattern ( elevated AST/ALT with normal ALP/GGT) suggests hepatitis, not biliary obstruction.
explanation_incorrect.C: Isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal ALP is Gilbert syndrome or another conjugation defect.
explanation_incorrect.D: Low albumin and prolonged PT reflect impaired synthetic function, not the cholestatic enzyme pattern of biliary disease.

educationalObjective: Cholestatic biliary disease shows elevated conjugated bilirubin, cholesterol, ALP, and GGT.
